newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble eases after disappointment at T-bill sales.
newsitem.headline: Rouble eases after disappointment at T-bill sales.

text.p: The rouble edged down on Thursday on an oversupplied market as banks disappointed by yesterday's Treasury bill auctions poured money back into the currency market, dealers said.
rouble/dollar Jan 30 midday Jan 30 early Jan 29 close

"Roubles are quite cheap," a dealer said. "Banks had looked forward to yesterday's T-bill auctions, but after the terms were changed, interest became lukewarm and a lot of roubles remained on the market."
Last week the Central Bank announced it would auction new T-bills on January 29, which would be subject to a new tax.
Dealers expected yields to rise in proportion to the tax and sold dollars to transfer roubles for the sales, the dealer said.
Banks had expected yields to rise to about 38 from 32 percent.

But on Tuesday the finance ministry announced it would issue two new tranches of old issues as the government had not yet decided on the rate of the tax. Some banks decided not to take part in the auctions as a result, the dealer said.
Dealers forecast the rouble would rise slightly tomorrow as banks needed the local currency to pay month-end taxes.
